summary: The Math object has square roots, powers, rounding, pi, and more. It is always available, so you never import it.
notes: Math.ceil(47 / 40) is 2 because it always rounds up. / gives 1.175 first, so no conversion is needed.
Math.round(-2.5) is -2, not -3, because halves always round toward the larger number.
pitfall: Writing math.sqrt(144) with a lowercase m causes ReferenceError: math is not defined. The object is Math.
contrast: JavaScript's Math object is always available like Java's Math class, so there is no import as in Python. Math.round() sends halves up (2.5 becomes 3), where Python's round(2.5) gives 2.
